messages:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] KV cache growth detected on runtime-prod-1 at 09:03 UTC. ContBatch inflight tokens rising above 2.4M. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: paging in. seeing latency p50->p99 jump on "mistral-13b" and "llama-70b" shards. any customer impact yet?

dmitri: support-ops reporting 2 customers with 504s and elevated token costs. stack: kv-continuous-batcher + prefix prefetch. suspect feedback loop with MQA tail tokens.

maya: attaching perf snippet:
```
metric: contbatch.inflight_tokens = 2_450_123
metric: kv.cache.insert_rate = 18_400/s
metric: kv.evictions = 0/s
mem.gpu0 = 89% (OOM risk)
```

oncall-sre: thanks. what's the query distribution? long tails?

eva: sample traces show large prefix fanout from llama-70b prompts that trigger high KV cardinality. Qwen fallback nodes also spiking due to routing.

olivia: customer impact: customerA (search-alt) seeing 25% error rate, customerB (chatbot) complaining latency 5s -> 18s. we need live mitigation and a customer comms draft.

oncall-sre: immediate plan: 1) reduce contbatch.max_tokens to 64 for Llama/Mistral runtime; 2) disable kv_prefetch for Llama model family; 3) add temporary circuit-breaker to reject requests >512 tokens for affected models; 4) roll hotfix to prod and monitor. ack? :pray:

dmitri: I'll prepare a runtime patch. quick config:
```
PATCH /runtime/configs/prod
{
  "model_filters": ["llama*","mistral*"],
  "contbatch_max_tokens": 64,
  "kv_prefetch_enabled": false,
  "max_request_tokens": 512
}
```

infra-deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline queued: runtime-config-hotfix-1766000000 -> staging -> canary(5%) -> prod. ETA ~6m.

maya: also setting KV eviction aggressive mode to ensure memory reclaimed:
```
curl -X POST https://infra/api/kv/evict -d '{"policy":"aggressive","target_percent":70}'
```

support-ops: starting customer notifications. Draft:
"We're seeing elevated latency and errors for certain Llama/Mistral workloads due to a KV/cache batching regression. We're rolling a configuration hotfix to mitigate and will follow up with a root cause." Suggestions?

olivia: add ETA: ~15m to mitigate, include temporary rate-limit guidance and mention no data-loss. good.

dmitri: canary applied. metrics look promising: inflight_tokens down to 600k, kv.insert_rate 4_200/s, GPU mem dropping to 64%.

oncall-sre: monitoring p99. still seeing occasional spikes on Qwen nodes—probably routed collateral. start throttling cross-model routing fallback to avoid cascade.

maya: applied route throttle: route.fallback_qwen.enabled=false for canary.

infra-deploy-bot: Canaries pass. Rolling to prod in 2m.

incidents-bot: [UPDATE] Hotfix rollout started at 09:12 UTC. Assigned incident severity: Sev3 -> observing.

support-ops: sent customerA update: "Hotfix rolling, expected stabilization in 15m. We'll follow up with detailed timeline." customerA replied :thumbsup: but asked for cost offset for spike.

dmitri: cost ask noted. we'll gather token burn numbers and hand to acct team.

oncall-sre: prod metrics show p99 back to baseline ~09:20 UTC, error rates dropping to 0.8% for customerA. keeping monitor for 30m window.

eva: root cause preliminary: combination of contbatch growth + prefix prefetch activating on high-cardinality llama prefixes created unbounded KV inserts; MQA tail tokens multiplied the inserts because of model output pattern for these customers. Working on a reproducible test.

olivia: postmortem owners? eva (root cause), dmitri (hotfix/patch), maya (mitigation configs), support-ops (customer comms)

support-ops: customerB followed up thanking team, asked for postmortem. we'll schedule a sync.

oncall-sre: closing incident channel in 45m if stable. final note: add a regression alert to catch contbatch.inflight_tokens > 1M for more than 2m next time.

incidents-bot: [RESOLVE] Resolved at 09:46 UTC. Incident ticket #INC-2026-1643 auto-updated.
